scenario: Alterion 技术面，面试官说「Design a system with separate read and write paths for a high-traffic DB.」你上来就想直接讲存储方案。
scenario_en: In an Alterion technical round the interviewer says, "Design a system with separate read and write paths for a high-traffic DB." Your instinct is to jump straight into storage.
q: 系统设计题一开口，第一句该怎么先立框架？
q_en: What should your very first line be to frame a system-design answer?
options: So for the for database, I'd separate the read pass and the write pass, so so if we want consistency, MySQL...
Okay so there's a lot here — SQL, NoSQL, a cache, a queue, it depends on so much, let me just start somewhere and see where it goes...
Before I design, let me lock the requirements and rough scale — read/write ratio, QPS, and consistency needs.
I shall commence by delineating the functional and non-functional requirements of the aforementioned system.
tradeoff: 先立需求+量级框架 vs 直接扎进存储细节：先框架多花十秒但后面每步都有依据；直接下钻省了那步，却让方案显得没章法。
why: 系统设计开口先锁需求和量级（读写比、QPS、一致性），它们决定后面每个选择；直接跳进存储或复读题目「read pass」，等于没框架就下钻。
why_en: Open by locking requirements and rough scale — read/write ratio, QPS, consistency — because they drive every later choice; don't dive into storage first.
whenOtherWins: 只有当面试官已经把需求和规模都给全了、明确说「直接给设计」时，才跳过澄清直接进方案。
options_en: So for the for database, I'd separate the read pass and the write pass, so so if we want consistency, MySQL...
Okay so there's a lot here — SQL, NoSQL, a cache, a queue, it depends on so much, let me just start somewhere and see where it goes...
Before I design, let me lock the requirements and rough scale — read/write ratio, QPS, and consistency needs.
I shall commence by delineating the functional and non-functional requirements of the aforementioned system.
optionMeanings: 直接扎进存储，还把 read path 说成「read pass」并结巴「so so」。
一上来罗列一堆技术，却不落地，说「随便开个头看看」。
先一句锁定需求和量级，再进设计。
用「I shall commence by delineating」的公文腔开场。
optionMeanings_en: Dives into storage, mangles "read path" to "read pass," stutters "so so."
Lists tech options up front but never anchors — "let me just start somewhere."
One line locking requirements and scale, then into design.
Opens in a stiff "I shall commence by delineating" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方还没听到框架，就看你陷进细节和口误。
显得没规划，面试官不知道你要往哪走。
面试官立刻看到你有章法，愿意跟你走下去。
过度正式，像念论文而不是设计讨论。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They hit your detail and the slip before hearing any frame.
Reads as no plan — they can't tell where you're headed.
They see structure immediately and follow your lead.
Over-formal — sounds like reading a paper, not designing.
optionDirectness: 错在没框架就下钻，还带「read pass」口误和卡顿。
错在罗列不收口，给了选项却没给顺序。
抓住「先需求+量级、再设计」这个开场骨架。
错在语域，设计讨论用书面公文体显得僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — drilling in with no frame, plus the "read pass" slip and stall.
Wrong — lists options with no order or priority.
Nails the opening arc: requirements and scale first, then design.
Wrong register — bureaucratese in a design chat feels stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读路径/写路径：请求进来后读操作和写操作各自经过的组件链路，常分开设计以便各自扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The read path and write path are the separate chains of components a read versus a write request flows through, often designed apart so each can scale on its own.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数，衡量系统承受的请求速率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS, Queries Per Second, measures how many requests the system handles each second.

scenario: Inventing VC 的技术轮，你刚澄清完需求，面试官点头等你往下推架构；上一次你在这里蹦出「choice front end high monitor design a whole API」这样的碎词。
scenario_en: In Inventing VC's technical round you've just finished clarifying requirements; the interviewer nods for you to move on. Last time you blurted fragments like "choice front end high monitor design a whole API."
q: 需求讲完，怎么把话头顺到高层架构？
q_en: With requirements done, how do you segue into the high-level design?
options: Okay, requirements are clear. Let me sketch the high-level design first — the main components and how a request flows through.
Choice front end, high monitor, like, design a whole API, targets, um, and then the backend...
So the DB is sharded by user ID with consistent hashing and a replication factor of three, and writes go through a leader, and the cache is write-through, and...
I will now enumerate the architectural components comprising the high-level system design.
tradeoff: 先给全景再下钻 vs 直接扎进某组件细节：先全景让对方有地图，代价是晚一点讲深；直接讲 sharding 细节省了铺垫，却让人抓不住整体。
why: 需求讲完先说「让我先勾出高层设计——主要组件和请求怎么流过」，给面试官一张地图，再逐块下钻；一上来就讲 sharding 细节会让人看不到全貌。
why_en: After requirements, say "let me sketch the high-level design first — the components and the request flow," giving them a map before you drill into any one box.
whenOtherWins: 只有当面试官明确说「跳过高层，直接讲你觉得最难的那块」时，才略过全景直接下钻某个组件。
options_en: Okay, requirements are clear. Let me sketch the high-level design first — the main components and how a request flows through.
Choice front end, high monitor, like, design a whole API, targets, um, and then the backend...
So the DB is sharded by user ID with consistent hashing and a replication factor of three, and writes go through a leader, and the cache is write-through, and...
I will now enumerate the architectural components comprising the high-level system design.
optionMeanings: 一句收束需求、再宣布勾画高层组件和请求流。
蹦碎词「choice front end, high monitor」拼不成句子。
跳过全景，直接扎进 sharding、replication 等深层细节。
用「I will now enumerate」的公文腔宣布组件。
optionMeanings_en: Closes requirements, then announces the high-level components and flow.
Blurts fragments — "choice front end, high monitor" — that don't form a sentence.
Skips the overview and dives into sharding, replication details.
Announces components in a stiff "I will now enumerate" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官拿到一张地图，知道接下来往哪听。
对方听到一堆名词碎片，抓不住你在说什么。
细节先行，对方还没有整体框架去挂这些细节。
过度正式，像宣读目录而不是讨论设计。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They get a map and know what to listen for next.
They hear noun fragments and can't parse your point.
Details first — they've no frame to hang them on yet.
Over-formal — like reading a table of contents.
optionDirectness: 抓住「先全景、再下钻」的过渡拍子。
错在语言崩成碎词，没有一个完整判断出口。
错在层级，跳过高层直接给最深的细节。
错在语域，设计过渡用公文体显得生硬。
optionDirectness_en: Nails the transition beat: overview first, then drill in.
Wrong — language breaks into fragments, no full statement lands.
Wrong altitude — skips the top level and gives the deepest detail.
Wrong register — a design segue in bureaucratese feels stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片：按某个键把数据切成多份分到不同节点，分摊读写压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data by a key across multiple nodes so each holds a slice and the load is spread.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性哈希：一种分片键映射方式，加减节点时只搬动少量数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps keys to nodes so that adding or removing a node moves only a small fraction of the data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复制因子：每份数据保存的副本数量，例如三副本抗单点故障。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The replication factor is how many copies of each piece of data are kept — e.g. three replicas to survive a node failure.

scenario: 系统设计轮时间过半，面试官说「We're low on time — pick the most interesting part and go deep.」你怕像之前那样越挑越乱、把思路挑丢。
scenario_en: Halfway through a design round the interviewer says, "We're low on time — pick the most interesting part and go deep." You're afraid of drifting and losing the thread like before.
q: 面试官让你挑一块深挖，怎么开口点题不跑偏？
q_en: When asked to pick one part to go deep, how do you open without drifting?
options: Um, so there's the cache, and the queue, and yeah, how about we go to the first idea, or maybe, let me think what I was...
The most interesting part is the write path — that's where the consistency tradeoff lives. Let me zoom in there.
So so the read pass is is the most, the most, in in the part that, that matters, so...
The component possessing the greatest technical significance shall now be examined in depth.
tradeoff: 主动点名最关键组件 vs 罗列一堆不下钻：点名让深挖有焦点，代价是放弃其它块；罗列显得全面，却把有限时间耗在挑不定上。
why: 时间紧时先一句点名「最有意思的是写路径，一致性取舍就在这」，立刻锁定焦点再深挖；把组件罗列一遍却挑不定，只会把宝贵时间耗光。
why_en: When time is short, name the target in one line — "the interesting part is the write path, that's where the consistency tradeoff lives" — then dive, instead of listing components and stalling.
whenOtherWins: 只有当面试官还没决定深挖哪块、明确让你「先列出候选再一起选」时，才先罗列组件而不马上锁定。
options_en: Um, so there's the cache, and the queue, and yeah, how about we go to the first idea, or maybe, let me think what I was...
The most interesting part is the write path — that's where the consistency tradeoff lives. Let me zoom in there.
So so the read pass is is the most, the most, in in the part that, that matters, so...
The component possessing the greatest technical significance shall now be examined in depth.
optionMeanings: 组件罗列一遍还挑不定，说「要不我们回第一个想法」丢了线。
一句点名写路径是焦点，理由是一致性取舍，再下钻。
结巴「so so、is is、in in」，句子挂在半空挑不出重点。
用「shall now be examined」的公文腔宣布要深挖。
optionMeanings_en: Lists components, can't decide, says "how about the first idea" — thread lost.
Names the write path as the focus, cites the consistency tradeoff, then dives.
Stutters "so so, is is, in in" — sentence dangles, no point emerges.
Announces the deep dive in a stiff "shall now be examined" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 时间被挑选耗掉，对方看你在原地绕。
焦点立刻锁定，剩下的时间全花在深度上。
对方只听到卡顿，等不到你选出哪一块。
过度正式，像宣读而不是选重点。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Time burns on choosing; they watch you circle in place.
Focus locks instantly and the rest of the time buys depth.
They hear only stalling, never which part you picked.
Over-formal — like an announcement, not picking a focus.
optionDirectness: 错在挑不定，罗列加丢线把时间耗空。
抓住「点名焦点+给理由+下钻」的深挖开场。
错在卡顿，句子停在原地没落到具体组件。
错在语域，选重点用公文体显得僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — can't commit; listing plus a lost thread drains the clock.
Nails the deep-dive opener: name the focus, give the reason, drill in.
Wrong — stalls in place; never lands on a concrete component.
Wrong register — picking a focus in bureaucratese feels stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写路径：一次写请求经过的组件链路，通常是一致性和持久化取舍的所在。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The write path is the chain of components a write request travels through, usually where consistency and durability tradeoffs live.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性取舍：为了更快或更可用，允许读到稍旧的数据 vs 保证读到最新写入之间的权衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The consistency tradeoff is the choice between always reading the latest write versus tolerating slightly stale reads for more speed or availability.

scenario: Gamma 后端面试，面试官问「What were the main tradeoffs?」上次你在这里说到「keeping simple and make the, make the system flexible」就卡进「sorry, let me think how to say」。
scenario_en: In a Gamma backend round the interviewer asks, "What were the main tradeoffs?" Last time you got to "keeping it simple and make the, make the system flexible" then stalled into "sorry, let me think how to say."
q: 面试官问主要取舍，怎么一句话架住框架？
q_en: When asked for the main tradeoffs, how do you frame it in one line?
options: One trade-off was between keeping it simple and make the, make the system flexible, so sorry, let me, let me think how to say...
There are so many tradeoffs honestly — consistency, latency, cost, complexity, flexibility — I could go through each for a while, where do you want me to start...
The principal tradeoff pertains to the dichotomy between simplicity and extensibility of the system.
The main tradeoff was simplicity versus flexibility — I went simple now, and here's what it costs us later.
tradeoff: 点名取舍轴+代价 vs 卡在措辞：一句「X vs Y，我选了 X，代价是…」既清晰又显成熟；卡在「how to say」把思考过程暴露成空白。
why: 讲取舍用固定公式「X versus Y，我选了 X，代价是…」：先点名两端，再说选哪端、代价是什么。卡在措辞或罗列一堆取舍都接不住。
why_en: Use the formula "the main tradeoff is X versus Y — I chose X, and here's the cost": name both poles, say which you picked, and own the price — don't stall on wording.
whenOtherWins: 只有当确实有多个同等重要的取舍、面试官也想听全时，才先列出取舍清单再逐条展开。
options_en: One trade-off was between keeping it simple and make the, make the system flexible, so sorry, let me, let me think how to say...
There are so many tradeoffs honestly — consistency, latency, cost, complexity, flexibility — I could go through each for a while, where do you want me to start...
The principal tradeoff pertains to the dichotomy between simplicity and extensibility of the system.
The main tradeoff was simplicity versus flexibility — I went simple now, and here's what it costs us later.
optionMeanings: 点到取舍就卡进「make the, make the」和「how to say」。
罗列一大串取舍却不选一个展开，反问对方从哪讲。
用「pertains to the dichotomy」的公文腔描述取舍。
一句点名「简单 vs 灵活」，说清选了哪端和代价。
optionMeanings_en: Reaches the tradeoff then stalls into "make the, make the" and "how to say."
Reels off many tradeoffs but commits to none, asking where to start.
Describes it in a stiff "pertains to the dichotomy" register.
Names "simple vs flexible," states which side and its cost.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方听到的是你在找词，不是你的判断。
铺得太广，面试官等不到一个明确取舍。
过度正式，像术语堆砌而非工程判断。
对方立刻听到清晰、成熟的权衡判断。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They hear you word-hunting, not your judgment.
Too broad — they never get one clear tradeoff.
Over-formal — jargon stack, not an engineering call.
They hear a clean, mature weighing of the tradeoff.
optionDirectness: 错在卡壳，取舍轴还没说完就断在措辞上。
错在铺太广，列了五个取舍却不落地一个。
错在语域，工程取舍用公文体显得空洞。
抓住「X vs Y + 选哪端 + 代价」的取舍公式。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — stalls; the tradeoff axis breaks off mid-wording.
Wrong — too broad; five tradeoffs listed, none committed to.
Wrong register — an engineering tradeoff in bureaucratese rings hollow.
Nails the formula: X vs Y, which side you chose, the cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 简单 vs 灵活：现在实现越简单越快上线，但未来扩展新场景就要改动更多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Simplicity versus flexibility: a simpler build ships faster now, but supporting new cases later takes more rework.

scenario: 系统设计轮，你在白板画好了框图，面试官说「Walk me through your diagram.」你怕像之前那样一个方框一个方框地念、越念越散。
scenario_en: In a design round you've drawn boxes on the whiteboard and the interviewer says, "Walk me through your diagram." You worry about naming box after box and drifting like before.
q: 怎么把画好的框图讲出声，让对方跟得上？
q_en: How do you narrate a finished diagram so the interviewer can follow?
options: Sure — a request hits the load balancer, goes to the API service, which reads cache and falls back to the DB. Let me trace one write.
So this is the, the API, and this box is is the, the database, and then the arrow, the arrow goes to, um...
Okay there are a lot of boxes here, this one connects to that one and also this one, arrows everywhere, let me see if I can remember what each of them does...
Observe the diagram: component one interfaces with component two, which subsequently transmits to component three.
tradeoff: 顺着请求流讲 vs 逐个念方框：跟着一次请求走让对方顺着数据流理解；逐个点名方框省事，却让人拼不出它们怎么串起来。
why: 讲框图别逐个念方框，跟着「一次请求怎么流过」走：负载均衡→API→缓存→回落数据库，再单独追一次写。数据流是面试官理解架构的主线。
why_en: Don't name boxes one by one — trace one request through: load balancer to API to cache, falling back to the DB, then follow a single write; the data flow is the thread they follow.
whenOtherWins: 只有当图里各组件相互独立、没有单一请求串起它们时，才逐个介绍组件而不走数据流。
options_en: Sure — a request hits the load balancer, goes to the API service, which reads cache and falls back to the DB. Let me trace one write.
So this is the, the API, and this box is is the, the database, and then the arrow, the arrow goes to, um...
Okay there are a lot of boxes here, this one connects to that one and also this one, arrows everywhere, let me see if I can remember what each of them does...
Observe the diagram: component one interfaces with component two, which subsequently transmits to component three.
optionMeanings: 跟着一次请求流讲：LB→API→缓存→回落 DB，再追一次写。
逐个指方框「this is the API, this box is is the DB」并卡在箭头。
感叹方框太多、箭头到处都是，还得回想每个干嘛。
用「component one interfaces with component two」的公文腔念图。
optionMeanings_en: Traces one request: LB to API to cache, falls back to DB, then a write.
Points at boxes — "this is the API, this box is is the DB" — stuck on an arrow.
Marvels at how many boxes and arrows, still recalling what each does.
Reads the diagram in a stiff "component one interfaces with two" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方顺着数据流走，一遍就看懂架构。
对方听到零散方框，拼不出整体怎么运转。
显得连自己的图都不熟，信心全无。
过度正式，像读框图说明书而非讲设计。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They ride the data flow and grasp the architecture in one pass.
They hear scattered boxes, can't assemble how it runs.
Looks like you don't know your own diagram — no confidence.
Over-formal — like reading a diagram manual, not explaining.
optionDirectness: 抓住「跟着一次请求走完数据流」的讲图主线。
错在逐个点方框，还卡在箭头上串不起来。
错在没主线，感叹方框多却不追任何一条流。
错在语域，讲图用公文体听着像说明书。
optionDirectness_en: Nails the narration thread: follow one request through the data flow.
Wrong — names boxes one by one and stalls on an arrow, nothing links.
Wrong — no thread; marvels at boxes without tracing any flow.
Wrong register — narrating a diagram in bureaucratese sounds like a manual.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负载均衡器：把进来的请求分摊到多台服务器，避免单台过载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer spreads incoming requests across multiple servers so no single one gets overloaded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存回落：先查缓存，命中就返回，未命中再去数据库取并回填缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache fallback means checking the cache first and, on a miss, reading from the database and filling the cache.

scenario: Amazon 电面 coding，你拿到一道 trie（前缀树）题。上一次在 Alterion 你直接闷头写、边写边嘟囔「so start with, then we return a list of str and prefix tree tree node」。
scenario_en: In an Amazon phone screen you get a trie (prefix-tree) problem. Last time at Alterion you dove straight in, muttering "so start with, then we return a list of str and prefix tree tree node."
q: 动手敲代码前，第一句该怎么说清思路？
q_en: Before you start typing, what's your first line to lay out the approach?
options: So let me see, so start with, then we return a list of str and prefix tree tree node, insert, okay, and then...
Okay, type in the parameter key, function, str, tree node, okay so it's a dict, and then we insert...
Let me talk through my approach first — I'll use a trie, insert char by char, then DFS from the prefix node.
Prior to implementation, I shall articulate my algorithmic strategy for the problem presently at hand.
tradeoff: 先讲思路再写 vs 闷头敲：先讲一句让面试官对齐方向、能早点纠偏；直接写省了开口，却把思路埋在键盘声里，错了也没人拦。
why: 写代码前先宣布「先讲思路再动手」，点名数据结构和步骤（trie、逐字符插入、从前缀 DFS），让面试官对齐；边写边嘟囔零碎词等于没讲。
why_en: Before coding, say "let me talk through my approach first" and name the data structure and steps — trie, insert char by char, DFS from the prefix node — so they can align, instead of muttering fragments as you type.
whenOtherWins: 题目极简单、或面试官说「直接写、边写边说」时，才跳过预讲直接开敲。
options_en: So let me see, so start with, then we return a list of str and prefix tree tree node, insert, okay, and then...
Okay, type in the parameter key, function, str, tree node, okay so it's a dict, and then we insert...
Let me talk through my approach first — I'll use a trie, insert char by char, then DFS from the prefix node.
Prior to implementation, I shall articulate my algorithmic strategy for the problem presently at hand.
optionMeanings: 闷头开写、嘟囔「prefix tree tree node」，没先讲思路。
边敲边念参数和类型当讲解，没给出算法结构。
先宣布要讲思路，再给出算法结构和步骤，然后才动手。
用「I shall articulate my algorithmic strategy」的公文腔开场。
optionMeanings_en: Dives in typing, mutters "prefix tree tree node" — no plan stated first.
Narrates params and types as "the plan" — "type in the parameter key, str."
Announces the plan first: trie, insert char by char, DFS from the prefix node.
Opens in a stiff "I shall articulate my algorithmic strategy" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官不知道你要写什么，错了也没法早拦。
对方听到的是键盘旁白，不是可评估的思路。
面试官提前对齐方向，能在写错前给你纠偏。
过度正式，像宣读方案而非结对编程。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They don't know what you're building; can't catch a wrong turn early.
They hear keyboard narration, not an evaluable plan.
They align on direction early and can steer you before a bug.
Over-formal — like reading a proposal, not pairing.
optionDirectness: 错在没预讲就开敲，思路埋在键盘声里。
错在把敲字过程当讲解，没给出算法结构。
抓住「先讲思路+点名数据结构和步骤」的编码开场。
错在语域，结对编码用公文体显得僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — types before explaining; the plan is buried in keystrokes.
Wrong — narrating typing isn't a plan; no algorithm structure given.
Nails the coding opener: state the plan, name the data structure and steps.
Wrong register — pairing in bureaucratese feels stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前缀树：一种按字符逐层展开的树，用来高效存取有公共前缀的字符串。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trie is a prefix tree that branches on each character, giving fast lookup and storage of strings that share prefixes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索：一条路走到底再回溯，常用来遍历树或图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS, Depth-First Search, explores one branch as deep as possible before backtracking — a common way to traverse a tree or graph.

scenario: 系统设计轮，面试官问「How big is this — walk me through the scale.」上次你憋着心算，只挤出「the scale is is in in terms of the traffic, but it's not about the traffic...」。
scenario_en: In a design round the interviewer asks, "How big is this — walk me through the scale." Last time you computed silently and only forced out "the scale is is in in terms of the traffic, but it's not about the traffic..."
q: 怎么把容量估算「说」出来，让面试官跟着你的数字走？
q_en: How do you narrate a scale estimate out loud so the interviewer can follow the numbers?
options: So the scale is is, in in terms of the traffic, but it's not, it's not about the traffic, but about the...
Let me do a quick back-of-the-envelope: say 200M daily users, 10% active at peak, so ~20M concurrent — that drives our fan-out.
There are lots of numbers we could estimate — users, requests, storage, bandwidth — it depends, let me just pick some and see what comes out...
I shall now undertake a quantitative estimation of the anticipated load parameters of the system.
tradeoff: 出声估算+落到设计 vs 憋着算或含糊：出声报公式让对方跟得上、还看到数字怎么用；憋着心算省了开口，却让思考过程变成一段空白。
why: 估算要出声报公式（200M 日活×10% 峰值≈20M 并发）、带单位、说清驱动什么（fan-out）。憋着心算或「about the traffic」都藏起推导。
why_en: Narrate the estimate as a formula — 200M daily users times 10% peak equals ~20M concurrent — with units and what it drives (fan-out); don't compute silently or wave at "the traffic."
whenOtherWins: 面试官说「规模先不用估、假设很大就行」时，才略过数字直接进设计。
options_en: So the scale is is, in in terms of the traffic, but it's not, it's not about the traffic, but about the...
Let me do a quick back-of-the-envelope: say 200M daily users, 10% active at peak, so ~20M concurrent — that drives our fan-out.
There are lots of numbers we could estimate — users, requests, storage, bandwidth — it depends, let me just pick some and see what comes out...
I shall now undertake a quantitative estimation of the anticipated load parameters of the system.
optionMeanings: 憋着心算，只挤出「is is、in in」这类卡顿和含糊。
出声把公式和单位报出来，算出并发量，再点名它驱动 fan-out。
罗列能估的一堆量却不落公式，说「随便挑几个看看」。
用「I shall now undertake a quantitative estimation」的公文腔。
optionMeanings_en: Computes silently, forcing out only "is is, in in, about the traffic."
Says the formula aloud: 200M daily times 10% peak ~ 20M concurrent, drives fan-out.
Lists estimable quantities but no formula — "let me just pick some."
Frames it in a stiff "I shall now undertake a quantitative estimation" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方只看到你卡住，看不到任何数字或推导。
面试官跟着数字走，还看到它怎么约束设计。
铺一堆待估项却无结论，对方等不到落点。
过度正式，像宣读而不是白板估算。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They see only a stall — no numbers, no reasoning.
They follow the numbers and see how it constrains the design.
Many quantities floated, no result — they get no landing.
Over-formal — like an announcement, not a whiteboard estimate.
optionDirectness: 错在憋着心算，出口只剩卡顿和含糊。
抓住估算叙述三拍：公式、单位、约束哪条设计。
错在只列待估项，不给公式也不给结论。
错在语域，白板估算用公文体显得僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — computing silently; only stalls and "about the traffic" come out.
Nails the estimate narration: formula aloud, units, and what it drives.
Wrong — lists quantities but gives no formula and no result.
Wrong register — a whiteboard estimate in bureaucratese feels stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 粗略估算：用几个近似数字快速算出量级，不求精确，只求数量级对。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A back-of-the-envelope estimate is a quick rough calculation using round numbers to get the order of magnitude, not an exact figure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 扇出：一次写入或事件需要推送/复制到很多下游（如关注者），量级直接决定负载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is when one write or event must be pushed to many downstream consumers (like followers); its size directly sets the load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 并发用户数：同一时刻在线活跃的用户数，是算服务器和连接数的基数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Concurrent users is how many are active at the same moment — the base figure for sizing servers and connections.
